recommendation: Add a single decision funnel page that shows the one open gate that blocks the most work, with the exact answer needed
evidence_that_it_helps: Eighteen flags and twenty decision gates currently have no ordering, so a reader cannot tell which one to answer first
options: A) Add the funnel page; B) keep separate registers; C) both, with the funnel on the home page
risk: A ranking is an editorial judgement and could be contested
depends_on_gate: None; publishing the ranking is itself the review artefact

recommendation: Replace the manual transcription with an approved API or a licensed feed
evidence_that_it_helps: Manual transcription is flagged as the weakest link, and the terms gate forbids systematic retrieval without consent
options: A) Request written permission then automate; B) licence a provider; C) keep manual transcription with a double-entry check
risk: Automating without permission would breach the terms the site already cites

recommendation: Adopt the official NFL gamebook as the starter-identity source and collect it weekly
evidence_that_it_helps: The gamebook is an official NFL document that lists the starting lineup, substitutions, Did Not Play and Not Active, and nineteen rows are already verified
options: A) Gamebook-only programme; B) gamebook plus a licensed participation feed; C) stay with designations only
risk: Gamebooks are PDFs and are not published as a machine-readable feed
review_status: For review — source verified, programme not started

recommendation: Record the previous week's gamebook starters as the pregame depth expectation instead of inventing a depth chart
improves_which_decision: Whether a lineup change can be modelled
evidence_that_it_helps: No official pregame depth chart exists, while the previous game's starters are official and already one week old when the next game kicks off
options: A) Previous-gamebook expectation; B) licensed depth-chart provider; C) leave depth unverified
risk: The previous game's lineup can change for reasons other than injury, so the expectation is noisy but not invented

recommendation: Publish a coverage matrix showing, for every official start slot, whether the Week 10 starter was confirmed, unknown or contradicted
evidence_that_it_helps: The site can show that a starter was out but not yet which slot was affected; the gamebook supplies slots such as LT, LG, C, RG and RT
options: A) Slot-level matrix; B) unit-level only; C) neither
risk: Slot mapping needs care because the gamebook lists five linemen while the report lists positions

recommendation: Split injury signals into absence and practice-trend families and test them separately before combining
evidence_that_it_helps: The report carries two different fields and they are not the same evidence, so pooling them hides which one carries information
options: A) Test separately then combine; B) combine immediately; C) use game status only
risk: Splitting doubles the number of tests and raises the multiplicity burden

recommendation: Declare rest designations as a separate category from injury and never pool them
evidence_that_it_helps: The Week 10 report contains explicit not-injury-related resting-player entries, which are a different process from an injury
options: A) Separate category; B) pool with injury; C) drop rest rows
risk: Dropping them would bias exposure counts

recommendation: Add a conflict register for cases where two official pages disagree, with the declared-source rule
evidence_that_it_helps: A verified case exists: the injury report lists Ben Brown as C while his official player page lists G
options: A) Conflict register; B) silently prefer one page; C) withhold conflicting rows
review_status: For review — one case already recorded

recommendation: Make the anti-luck suite a hard gate rather than a report: no leaderboard row without a bootstrap interval and a search log
evidence_that_it_helps: NIST guidance on the bootstrap and on multiple comparisons explains why a point estimate and an unadjusted best-of-N cannot separate skill from chance
options: A) Hard gate; B) advisory report; C) neither
risk: A hard gate delays any leaderboard until enough data exists, which is the correct outcome but a slower one
review_status: For review — rules written, not enforced

recommendation: Show the uncertainty interval and the eligible N in the same cell as every score, and refuse to sort ties
evidence_that_it_helps: Ordering overlapping intervals invents precision the sample does not have
options: A) Interval in the cell with no sort on overlap; B) interval in a tooltip; C) point estimate only
risk: Wider tables are harder to scan on a phone

recommendation: Add a what-changed-since-the-last-snapshot page generated from git history rather than prose
evidence_that_it_helps: Every change to a value is already a commit, and surfacing it makes silent edits visible
options: A) Generate from git log; B) hand-written changelog; C) neither
risk: Git history is not a data audit and could be mistaken for one

recommendation: Publish a coverage score per page: how many rows have a source link, how many are blank and how many are flagged
evidence_that_it_helps: The site claims a source per row but does not show the ratio of verified to unverified cells
options: A) Per-page coverage score; B) one site-wide score; C) neither
risk: A single percentage can hide a badly sourced page
review_status: For review — partially available from the build checks

recommendation: Run a second, independent transcription pass and publish the disagreement rate as a number
evidence_that_it_helps: The current check compares the transcription with a second transcription made in the same session, which does not detect a shared misreading
options: A) Independent second transcriber; B) same-session second pass; C) no second pass
risk: Requires a second person or an approved tool

recommendation: Freeze a preregistration file before any evaluation and refuse to score a strategy without one
evidence_that_it_helps: Choosing the metric after seeing the result is the most common way a backtest becomes fiction
options: A) Preregistration file per strategy; B) one programme-level document; C) none

recommendation: Commission a written legal opinion on rewards, advertising and jurisdiction before any reward is described
improves_which_decision: Whether a leaderboard can have prizes
evidence_that_it_helps: Official Japanese guidance treats sports betting as a criminal offence and prohibits advertising or guiding users to it; that is Japan-specific and does not decide other designs
options: A) Written opinion; B) rely on the current disclaimer; C) drop rewards
risk: Cost and time, and the answer may be no

recommendation: Decide the product scope in writing and remove any page that does not fit it
evidence_that_it_helps: The current site mixes research, a possible product and a possible contest, which multiplies the open questions
options: A) Research only; B) private decision tool; C) published product
risk: Narrowing scope may remove features you wanted

recommendation: Add a plain-language statement on every page of what that page cannot tell you
evidence_that_it_helps: A reader can mistake a verified injury count for a verified betting edge
options: A) One-line limitation on every page; B) a single limitations page; C) both
risk: Repeating limits can bury the finding

recommendation: Add an accessible, dependency-free chart for the exposure counts instead of only tables
evidence_that_it_helps: Tables are filterable, but the distribution across twenty-eight teams is hard to see in rows
options: A) Inline SVG bars generated by the build; B) an external chart library; C) tables only
risk: No third-party dependency should be added because the build has none
